scenario.title: Elements: A River Worth Returning To
scenario.premise: Starting from four storybook elements, travel from an orchard to a coastal gathering. Make useful things for people you meet. The world remembers what you leave behind.

stage.title: Four beginnings
stage.speaker: The keeper
stage.motivation: The river gathering is a month away. We begin with earth, water, air and fire. Make a bowl for supper and bricks for a hearth.
stage.travelText: Our next stop: Four beginnings. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

things.label: Earth
things.description: Loose ground: mineral grit, clay and the material in which roots grow.

things.label: Water
things.description: Flowing, soaking and carrying; a liquid that takes the shape of its container.

things.label: Air
things.description: The invisible moving world around us. It carries moisture and feeds a flame.

things.label: Fire
things.description: Heat and light. It cooks, hardens and changes materials rather than merely joining them.

stage.title: Food for the crossing
stage.speaker: The shore cook
stage.motivation: There is no hearth on the crossing. Make smoked fish and a jar of pickles for the boats, not just another pretty table.
stage.travelText: Our next stop: Food for the crossing. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

areas.label: A light to come home to

things.label: Air
things.description: The invisible moving world around us. It carries moisture and feeds a flame.

things.label: Fire
things.description: Heat and light. It cooks, hardens and changes materials rather than merely joining them.

things.label: Fruit
things.description: Ripe, juicy produce with flesh around its seeds.

things.label: Wood
things.description: Rough timber: solid lengths with grain and bulk, not flat boards yet.

things.label: Thread
things.description: A long, fine strand spun from fibers; useful for binding and stitching.

things.label: Rope
things.description: Thicker cordage that can hold a load or keep larger pieces together.

things.label: Jar
things.description: A hollow clay container with a narrower opening than a bowl.

things.label: Cider
things.description: A fermented fruit drink, no longer the fresh juice it began as.

locations.label: Tidal shore
locations.description: Brackish pools and the fishery beside the sea.

output.message: Feast table. The communal tiled table laid with the shared meal. People have pulled up their stools; there is a place for you among them. The cook ladles porridge while a visitor passes the compote. Neighbours make room at the laid table, and you sit down among the people you have been making things for. Across the water someone tries the flute; this is the gathering, not a rehearsal.

args: Stopped satisfied after the shared feast at stage 24. Food for the crossing was coherent with one hint. Visitors using the washstand and sitting together at the feast gave the making a purpose. Washstand required plain bowl instead of glazed bowl; water bottle filling failed until a lid made an urn; these felt arbitrary. Soap was clear but routine. Kitchen needed a hint to discover cooking pot, then an explicit reverse-direction correction because grain rather than pot was at the hearth. I liked bringing fruit to the pot once the pot was placed. Compote plus porridge made a feast but also removed untouched bread, which surprised me. A gift for winter is mildly interesting, but the meal is a satisfying stopping point. Logical player interface only, not native UI evidence.
